provenance: Authored implementation guidance; not extracted Figma policy and not yet approved by the DS owner.

usage: Use to identify a person beside a name; do not encode account status in the portrait.
Keep an explicit name or fallback when no portrait is available.
accessibility: Decide whether the portrait adds information beyond the adjacent name; review its text alternative.
If the avatar opens a profile, label and test the enclosing link rather than making the image an unnamed action.

usage: Treat bg and overlay as separate owners, not interchangeable surfaces.
The overlay Device axis is visual evidence only; modal behavior belongs to the consuming pattern.
accessibility: Decorative surfaces must not receive keyboard focus.
Check foreground text and focus visibility against every surface in its actual composition.

usage: Show concise status or classification; do not make every badge clickable.
Keep badge-tier level separate from feedback states; confirm business tier meanings with the owner.
accessibility: Express status in text, not color alone.
If status changes dynamically, decide whether a non-disruptive announcement is needed; test it in context.

usage: Use the bottom-shet owner for the sheet and its contextual button owner for the action stack.
Do not replace the contextual button identity with the Core Button simply because its name matches.
accessibility: If modal, provide a name, move focus inside, contain Tab navigation, support Escape and restore focus.
Do not mark a non-modal sheet aria-modal; confirm the intended interaction before implementation.

usage: Represent ancestor locations, not a history of every visited page.
Use page02/page03 visibility properties only for the corresponding hierarchy levels.
accessibility: Use a named navigation region and identify the current page.
Make ancestor destinations real links; exclude decorative separators from accessible names.

usage: Use a button for an action and a link for navigation.
Select only actual source variants; an API axis list does not guarantee every possible combination exists.
accessibility: Test activation with both Enter and Space and provide an accessible name, including icon-only actions.
Verify disabled behavior and focus placement after the action. A Figma hover state is not keyboard evidence.

usage: Use for independent selections; use a radio group for mutually exclusive choices.
Preserve legacy instances. The preferred candidate adds error, disabled, indeterminate and on-dark variants.
accessibility: Associate each checkbox with its label and test Space toggling.
Expose mixed state correctly and name related checkbox groups.

usage: Use container as the Core composition surface; swap-content is a separate content owner.
Do not rename this primitive to a new Core Card API.
accessibility: Choose semantics from the contained content, not from the visual box.
Keep a logical heading order and avoid unnecessary focus stops on static surfaces.

usage: Use Calendar for date selection only after confirming date format, range and timezone requirements.
The three source states do not specify a complete calendar interaction model.
accessibility: Specify and test grid keyboard navigation, current date, selected date and focus return.
Name the date field and expose format instructions; test text entry and invalid dates as well as the popup.

usage: Use horizontal or vertical variants to separate content groups.
Do not use a divider instead of a meaningful heading or label.
accessibility: Decide whether separation is semantic or purely decorative.
Do not make a static divider keyboard-focusable or imply it is a draggable splitter.

usage: Keep input-text and dropdown identities and APIs separate.
Document read-only, disabled, validation and chip states explicitly; a hidden label must not remove the field name.
accessibility: Associate labels and supporting/error text with the actual input.
Test text entry, clear actions and error announcements; choose a combobox pattern only when its interaction is actually implemented.

usage: Use basic, checkbox and no-result variants according to the task.
Do not silently migrate the legacy Checkbox used by existing list compositions.
accessibility: Choose list, listbox or checkbox-group semantics from the actual behavior.
Test each actionable row and disabled option; a visual selected state alone is not a selection API.

usage: Choose the exact sidebar, header, mobile navigation or search owner by key.
Keep navigation destinations distinct from filter and notification actions.
accessibility: Name navigation regions and expose the current destination.
Test expand/collapse state, focus order and all mobile controls; ordinary site links do not require menu roles.

usage: Use for one selection within a named group.
Retain literal legacy values such as fasle at the source boundary; do not silently rename an existing instance.
accessibility: Give the group and each option accessible names.
Test Space and arrow-key selection, checked state and disabled behavior.

usage: Document source positions without assigning new meaning to Property 1.
Prefer native scrolling unless an approved custom scrolling behavior is supplied.
accessibility: Verify keyboard access to overflowing content and visible focus.
Do not turn a decorative scroll indicator into an unimplemented scrollbar widget.

usage: Distinguish the tab/chip, Switch tab, divider-tab and composed tab owners.
Use tab semantics only for switching associated panels, not merely because a control resembles a tab.
accessibility: Associate tabs with panels and expose which tab is selected.
Test arrow navigation, Tab order, activation and the disabled state for the selected activation model.

usage: Use for an on/off setting whose label describes the setting.
The two visual states do not define saving, loading or failure behavior; specify these in the product.
accessibility: Keep the accessible label stable while changing the checked state.
Test Space activation and report on/off programmatically.

usage: Use for supplemental information, not the only copy of essential instructions.
The source includes an optional text-link; confirm whether this requires a popover rather than tooltip semantics.
accessibility: A tooltip should work on focus as well as hover and dismiss with Escape.
Interactive content needs a different focus/interaction pattern; do not put a focusable link inside a standard tooltip.
